explanation: The closest Mathlib result is the instance `HasEnoughRootsOfUnity (ZMod p) (p - 1)` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/ZMod/Torsion.lean`, which needs `[Fact p.Prime]` and covers only `d = p - 1`. To reach an arbitrary `d ∣ p - 1`, the library combines that instance with `HasEnoughRootsOfUnity.of_dvd` and `HasEnoughRootsOfUnity.exists_isPrimitiveRoot`, after setting up `Fact p.Prime` and `NeZero (p - 1)`. That chains several declarations, which is more than the allowed glue. Searches covered: `HasEnoughRootsOfUnity` and `exists_isPrimitiveRoot` across Mathlib; statements of the form `∃ ζ, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n`; hypotheses `∣ p - 1` and `∣ Fintype.card F - 1`; `IsPrimitiveRoot` with `card` or `p - 1` arguments; and the `FieldTheory/Finite`, `RingTheory/RootsOfUnity` and `NumberTheory/MulChar` directories. No single declaration states that `ZMod p` (or a finite field) has a primitive `d`-th root of unity for every `d ∣ p - 1`.
